newsitem.title: USA: Photocomm says deal sours with ACX.
newsitem.headline: Photocomm says deal sours with ACX.

text.p: Photocomm Inc., a major maker of wireless solar electric power systems, said Thursday it has been unable to close a deal in which ACX Technologies Inc. had agreed to acquire a majority stake in the company.
Photocomm said its board decided that ACX's proposal is inadequate, "at least pending additional clarification."

The companies announced Aug. 21 that ACX had agreed in principle to purchase 2,000,000 new issue shares of Scottsdale, Ariz.-based Photocomm. Together with a previously announced plan for ACX to acquire 6.6 million Photocomm shares from the New World Power Corp., ACX would have ended up with a 51 percent stake in Photocomm.
Photocomm said ACX has been unresponsive to requests for specific information about its potential majority stake, and Photocomm's future plans and strategies.
Golden, Colo.-based ACX could not be immediately reached for comment. The company applies innovative technology to manufacture value-added industrial products, such as ceramics and packaging.
Photocomm's stock rose 12.5 cents to $2.625 on Nasdaq at mid-morning. ACX was unchanged at $16.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.
